migration.description: Persist Host-scoped Codex source notification identities and acknowledgement state for reconnect-safe replay.

compatibility_assessment.reason: The migration adds a durable source-event acknowledgement table without changing existing REST or MCP payloads.

durable_state.description: Source event identities, raw payloads and applied or failed acknowledgement state survive process restart and reconnect replay.
durable_state.storage_implementation: PostgreSQL table and recovery index managed by the embedded Goose application migration history.

source_compatibility_range.from_program_versions: Codex source synchronization candidate containing migration 00022.
source_compatibility_range.to_program_version: Codex source synchronization repair candidate containing migration 00023.
source_compatibility_range.compatibility_boundary: Older candidates ignore this table and do not provide durable source-event acknowledgement.

ordered_operations.description: Create the Host-scoped source event identity, raw payload and acknowledgement state table.
Add a recovery index for pending and failed source events.

database_migration.backfill: none; existing source notifications have no trustworthy durable identity and are not guessed into the new table.
rollout_signals: A source notification is acknowledged to the Connector only after its durable event state is applied.
A repeated event identity is read from the table and does not apply its side effect twice.

validation: Fresh and upgraded PostgreSQL databases apply migration 00023 with the Host foreign key and recovery index.
A repeated source event identity remains applied without replaying the title or source-status side effect.
A concurrent duplicate cannot enter processing while the first durable event handler owns the identity; interrupted processing is reopened during Server startup recovery.
